# ReARM readiness rules (ReARM Pro), rule set 5

<!-- Generated by ReARM's readiness rule list test from the rules ReARM runs. Do not edit: a changed copy fails the documentation image build. -->

The rules ReARM checks a draft of a regulatory package against, in the order ReARM evaluates them.

This list is rule set 5. The number is the `ruleSetVersion` of a Final version's check summary and of the `checkSummary` in its manifest: it names the rules that judged the version. The checking engine's FDA checker rules are another list, with its own number, read in the version's **Check report** part.

A must-fix row that is not passed refuses Confirm and Finalize; a review row never does. A row that could not be evaluated refuses both, whatever its severity.

The same number means the same rules: the number changes whenever this list changes and whenever a rule is changed to decide differently on some draft.

This list says what ReARM checks and when a row passes. It is not a statement that a package which passes meets a regulator's expectations.

| Row | Rule | Label | Severity | Passes when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `SBOM_AUTHOR` | SBOM author | must-fix | the engine check `fda.baseline.author-name` is `PASS` in the check made at the last rebuild |
| 2 | `SBOM_TIMESTAMP` | SBOM timestamp | must-fix | the engine check `fda.baseline.timestamp` is `PASS` in the check made at the last rebuild |
| 3 | `SBOM_SUPPLIER` | Supplier name | must-fix | the engine check `fda.baseline.supplier-name` is `PASS` in the check made at the last rebuild |
| 4 | `SBOM_COMPONENT_NAME` | Component name | must-fix | the engine check `fda.baseline.component-name` is `PASS` in the check made at the last rebuild |
| 5 | `SBOM_VERSION` | Component version | must-fix | the engine check `fda.baseline.version-string` is `PASS` in the check made at the last rebuild |
| 6 | `SBOM_HASH` | Component hash | must-fix | the engine check `fda.baseline.component-hash` is `PASS` in the check made at the last rebuild |
| 7 | `SBOM_IDENTIFIER` | Unique identifier | must-fix | the engine check `fda.baseline.unique-identifier` is `PASS` in the check made at the last rebuild |
| 8 | `SBOM_RELATIONSHIP` | Dependency relationships | must-fix | the engine check `fda.baseline.relationship` is `PASS` in the check made at the last rebuild |
| 9 | `SUPPORT_LEVEL` | Level of support | must-fix | the engine check `fda.component.support-level` is `PASS` in the check made at the last rebuild |
| 10 | `SUPPORT_END_DATE` | End-of-support date | must-fix | the engine check `fda.component.end-of-support` is `PASS` in the check made at the last rebuild |
| 11 | `SUPPORT_CLAIM_CONFLICT` | Support claims agree | review | no attested component of the release says the level of support actively maintained together with the end-of-support reason community project, no support commitment |
| 12 | `VENDORED_UNDESCRIBED` | Vendored code described | must-fix | no component of the release SBOM the build pinned is without an identifier (a package URL, a `bom-ref` that is a package URL, or a CPE); a component marked `reliza:support:selfComponent` is not counted |
| 13 | `COVER_SUMMARY` | Cover summary | must-fix | the release's own cover summary is not empty and differs from the organization's default cover summary, both read with white space at either end removed |
| 14 | `DEVICE_DATES` | Device support dates | review | the component's medical profile declares both the device end-of-support date and the device end-of-life date |
| 15 | `OPTIONAL_PARTS_OFF` | Optional parts | review | the component is not a product, or the build produced or referenced every part its package kind lists as optional |
| 16 | `VULN_KEV_UNASSESSED` | Known exploited (KEV) findings are assessed | must-fix | an enabled KEV catalog of the organization (CISA KEV when it is enabled, else VulnCheck KEV) has synchronized at least once, however long ago, and every finding of the release that any KEV source of the organization lists or has listed as known exploited (a source since turned off and an entry since withdrawn included), suppressed findings included, has a complete assessment (see Every finding has an assessment) and a written explanation; a listed finding on a component without a package URL is never passed |
| 17 | `VULN_FINDING_UNASSESSED` | Every finding has an assessment | must-fix | every finding of the release, suppressed findings included, has an assessment recorded in ReARM (a state that only a scanner reports is none) that is not in triage and names a discovery method; a finding assessed as not affected or false positive also has a justification or an explanation, a resolved finding an explanation, and an exploitable finding a risk level, at least one risk control, a response, recommendation or workaround, a residual risk conclusion (acceptable or not acceptable) and the rationale for it; an explanation, recommendation, workaround or rationale of white space only is none; a finding on a component without a package URL is never passed |
| 18 | `VULN_KEV_AFFECTS_DEVICE` | Known exploited (KEV) findings that affect the device | review | no known exploited finding of the release whose assessment is complete with its explanation (see Known exploited (KEV) findings are assessed) is assessed as exploitable |

Rows 1 to 10: an engine check that is `FAIL` or `NOT_ASSESSED` leaves its row not passed; any other status, or a check that does not hold the engine check, is a row that could not be evaluated.

Each of these ten rows is a review item, not a pass, when the engine passes the check while no component meets it, because every component it counts is justified.

The dependency relationships row is a review item, not a pass, when ReARM linked components that the SBOM gave no dependency relationship under the node that holds them.
